Remote Sensing · GIS · Environmental Assessment

Multi-Temporal Environmental Assessment of Lake Murray, Australia

Remote Sensing GIS Environmental Assessment

Multi-Temporal Environmental Assessment of Lake Murray, Australia Using Landsat 8/9 and GIS

📅 Study Period: 2014 · 2018 · 2021 · 2024

This project presents a multi-temporal environmental assessment of Lake Murray, Australia, using Landsat 8/9 satellite imagery and ArcGIS Pro. The analysis evaluates vegetation dynamics, water extent, water turbidity, and surface water temperature between 2014 and 2024, providing a comprehensive picture of how the lake's ecosystem has evolved over the past decade.

🎯 Objectives

  • Monitor vegetation changes using NDVI
  • Detect surface water changes using NDWI
  • Improve water extraction using MNDWI
  • Assess water turbidity using NDTI
  • Analyze Surface Water Temperature (SWT)
  • Compare environmental changes from 2014 to 2024

🛰 Data Sources

  • USGS Earth Explorer
  • Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2
  • Landsat 9 Collection 2 Level-2

💻 Software & Platforms

  • ArcGIS Pro
  • Spatial Analyst

📍 Study Area

Lake Murray, situated along the lower reaches of the Murray River system in South Australia, is a vital freshwater and estuarine ecosystem bordered by Strathalbyn, Wellington, Milang, Clayton Bay, and Meningie. Its water extent, riparian vegetation, and thermal regime are highly sensitive to seasonal inflows, land-use pressure, and climate variability — making it an ideal setting for multi-temporal remote sensing analysis.

🧭 Results & Project Highlights

Five multi-temporal comparisons — captured in 2014, 2018, 2021, and 2024 — trace the trajectory of vegetation density, surface water extent, turbidity, and thermal conditions across Lake Murray over the decade.

ArcGIS Pro Google Earth Engine Landsat NDBI

Urban Growth Monitoring in Madrid, Spain (2013–2025)

This project investigates urban growth patterns in Madrid, Spain between 2013 and 2025 using Landsat imagery and the Normalized Difference Built-up Index (NDBI). The study evaluates spatial urban expansion and identifies development hotspots using multi-temporal change detection techniques.

Outputs

  • Urban expansion mapped successfully
  • Growth hotspots identified
  • Built-up area changes quantified

Remote Sensing Projects

Environmental Monitoring Deep Dive

Remote Sensing Environmental Monitoring Water Quality

Spatiotemporal Assessment of Water Quality Dynamics in the Dead Sea Using Remote Sensing Techniques (2013–2025)

📅 Study Period: 2013 · 2016 · 2019 · 2022 · 2025

This project focuses on monitoring and analyzing water quality changes in the Dead Sea between 2013 and 2025 using multi-temporal Landsat satellite imagery. The study integrates water extent mapping, turbidity assessment, and surface temperature analysis to evaluate environmental changes and water quality dynamics over time.

🎯 Objectives

  • Monitor temporal changes in the Dead Sea water extent
  • Assess relative turbidity levels using remote sensing indices
  • Analyze surface water temperature variations
  • Investigate long-term environmental changes between 2013 and 2025

🛰 Data Sources

  • Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS
  • Landsat 9 OLI-2/TIRS-2
  • USGS EarthExplorer

💻 Software & Platforms

  • ArcGIS Pro
  • Google Earth Engine (GEE)

⚙ Methodology

01Data acquisition and preprocessing
02Water body extraction using NDWI
03Turbidity assessment using NDTI
04Surface temperature retrieval using SST
05Temporal analysis for 2013, 2016, 2019, 2022, 2025
06Statistical comparison and trend analysis
07Map production and visualization

📊 Key Indicators

NDWI — Water Index NDTI — Turbidity Index SST — Surface Temperature

📤 Key Outputs

  • Water Extent Maps
  • Turbidity Distribution Maps
  • Sea Surface Temperature Maps
  • Temporal Trend Analysis
  • Environmental Change Assessment
  • Professional GIS Layouts & Cartographic Outputs
